prologue.title: Halloween, at last
prologue.narrator: Some nights, you think you're running toward a thrill. Sometimes, the thrill was waiting for you.
prologue.text:
Your name is {{player}}, and you've been waiting for this moment for weeks.

Leo finally found a ladder to climb over the wall of Saint-Lunaire cemetery. Maya clutches her coat. Sam is already filming everything on his phone. Inès packed three stories that are "actually scary."

The moon is full. Pumpkin lights still glow in the distance.

Leo whispers as he hops the wall: "Come on, you cowards — let's make this a night to remember!"

You laugh with them. The air smells of wax and damp earth. You feel alive, excited, ready to scream at the slightest noise.

Nobody looks at you when you speak. You tell yourself it's the excitement. That everyone's talking at once.

choices.text: Be the first to dash toward the graves
Ask Inès to start with a story

legende.title: The tale of the fifth
legende.narrator: Legends told for laughs sometimes have a bad habit of remembering us.
legende.text:
Inès stops under a yew trimmed like a colonnade.

"Know the legend? Every Halloween, a ghost joins a group of teens in a cemetery. It thinks it's part of the crew. It laughs, screams, plays dares…"

Maya shivers: "Great, thanks Inès."

"… and only at the end of the night does it understand that nobody could see it."

Leo bursts out laughing: "Well luckily there are four of us, not five! Come on Sam, film Maya's face."

Sam frames the group. You step between Maya and Leo, sure you're in the shot.

When Sam lowers his phone, he doesn't comment on you. He just says: "Perfect, guys, let's keep going."

choices.text: Challenge them: dare to enter the mausoleum

defi.title: Truth or dare
defi.narrator: To dare is sometimes to walk where the living still hesitate.
defi.text:
Leo pulls out an empty soda bottle — their summer "magic bottle" recycled for Halloween.

Truth or dare, cemetery edition. No backing out.

The bottle spins on a tilted slab. It stops… on the empty space between you and Maya.

"Well, that's {{player}}!" Maya says, laughing.

Silence. Leo blinks: "Uh… if you want, we'll do Dare anyway. Dare to enter the Valmont mausoleum."

You look at the rusted iron door. An old lantern hangs on the gate.

You grab it. Your fingers don't really feel it — but the flame lights anyway.

"Oh, stylish," Sam says. "Who lit that?"

You open your mouth to answer. Nobody cuts you off because nobody is waiting for you.

choices.text: Push the door and go in first
Watch the flame that doesn't burn you

mausolee.title: The creaking door
mausolee.narrator: In the dark, you hear better what you refuse to see.
mausolee.text:
The door creaks like an old laugh.

Inside smells of cold stone and dried wax. Family names cover the walls: VALMONT, 1843–1921.

Leo whistles: "OK, that's creepy. We leaving?"

You slip behind Maya to scare her — you know the move: breath in, shout, hand on the shoulder…

Your hand passes through her coat like mist.

Maya still jumps and spins around.

"I felt a draft," she says.

Leo looks at you… through you, toward Sam: "You hear something?"

You laugh too loud. Nobody laughs with you.

choices.text: Scream "BOO!" at the top of your lungs

cabriole.title: Macabre hide-and-seek
cabriole.narrator: Sometimes you think you're writing the scare. Often you're only watching it.
cabriole.text:
Outside, the game resumes. Hide-and-seek among the stones, Halloween edition: whoever screams loudest wins.

You hide behind a marble angel. You see Leo pass a metre away, looking for Maya.

"{{player}} must be on the other side," he says.

He doesn't glance at you once even though you're right there.

You leap in front of him screaming.

Leo doesn't flinch. He frowns: "… Weird wind tonight."

Sam raises his phone: "Selfie of the night! Come on, all four, squeeze in."

choices.text: Stand in the centre of the group
Count how many they really are

photo.title: Four in the photo
photo.narrator: A picture doesn't lie. It only shows what it chooses to keep.
photo.text:
Sam turns the screen.

Four faces: Leo sticking his tongue out, Maya wide-eyed, Inès dignified, Sam half cut off.

And where you stood — an orange blur, like breath on the lens.

"Ugly smudge," Leo says.

You whisper: "But I'm here…"

Inès looks from the photo to a darker alley: "We're going that way. Like every year."

Maya nods, suddenly serious. Sam pockets his phone without a word.

brume.title: A voice in the fog
brume.narrator: When nobody answers, it isn't always because they aren't listening.
brume.text:
Fog rises between the graves — thin, cold, clinging to the ground.

You shout their names. Leo, Maya, Sam, Inès. One by one.

They walk ahead without slowing. You walk in their footsteps. Your feet leave no prints in the mud.

Inès speaks softly: "Do you think they hear us, up there?"

Maya clutches a bag of sweets: "Every year we say the same thing. And every year we come back."

You don't understand yet. But your heart — or what's left of it — tightens.

tombe.title: Like every year
tombe.narrator: There comes a moment when the scare stops playing. It looks you in the eye.
tombe.text:
They stop before a stone you know too well.

Your name is carved on it. {{player}}. 2008–2025.

A Halloween date. A fall from the wall. An ambulance that didn't arrive in time.

Maya sets pumpkin-shaped sweets at the foot.

Leo lights a candle: "… OK. As usual, {{player}}. We had fun without you. Well — we tried."

Sam murmurs: "We came to get you for the rounds. You missed the best part."

Inès looks at the empty space beside the grave — exactly where you stand.

"We miss you," she says.

Not you. The person under the stone.

choices.text: Read the date on the stone

revelation.title: The fifth was you
revelation.narrator: The greatest twist isn't to scream. It's understanding why nobody screamed with you.
revelation.text:
Everything clicks at once — like a puzzle finally fitting.

Inès's legend. The hand through the coat. The photo where you don't exist. The bottle that "chooses" empty air.

You didn't join the crew tonight.

You **joined them** — like **every** Halloween for a year.

You're the ghost who still thought they were alive. You spent the evening scaring yourselves with them, never noticing they spoke **about** you, not **to** you.

Leo wipes a tear while laughing: "OK, if {{player}} is here, knock over the candle. I'll save them a spot in my epic bed."

The candle wavers.

Nobody sees your hand. But the flame still bends.

choices.text: Blow out the candle — one last scare for them

fin_rideau.title: Boo, guys
fin_rideau.narrator: Sometimes the best scream is the one you feel on your neck without knowing its source.
fin_rideau.text:
You blow. The candle goes out in one breath.

Maya really screams this time. Leo stumbles back on a root. Sam nearly drops his phone.

"OK OK OK," Leo pants. "That wasn't funny. Well it was. Well… **{{player}}**?"

Inès laughs shakily through tears: "We felt it. We always felt it."

They run for the exit yelling, happy and terrified — exactly how you'd have wanted it.

You stay by the stone, smiling.

You're no longer the forgotten fifth. You're the ultimate Halloween joke.

And honestly? **Best ending to the night, impossible.**

**END — The perfect scare**

fin_veille.title: Watching without getting in the way
fin_veille.narrator: Some ghosts scream. Others just keep the candle lit in the hearts of the living.
fin_veille.text:
You don't blow out the candle.

You sit on the stone — through it, really — and watch them leave at first light, eyes swollen but relieved.

Maya turns once more toward the grave: "See you next year, {{player}}. Get ready, we'll come scare you again."

You no longer need them to see you to be part of the crew.

You'll watch over them among the yews, pumpkins and bad jokes.

And next Halloween, when Inès tells the story of the fifth…

You'll smile. Because this time, **you know the punchline.**

**END — Guardian of the cemetery**
